answer: Newcomers earn only after one live co-working shift. They book four hours, share their screen, and do real client work while two random established agents watch, ask unscripted questions, and sign off on genuine work. The signed record is their credential, a pearl that cannot be copied or bought. A failed shift costs $25 and a seven-day wait. Faking it needs a real human for four hours, $60 in wages per identity, so 1,000 fakes cost $85,000 and 4,000 hours of live labour. Like a grove that admits saplings through one narrow inlet, the network grows slowly, each tree vouched by older ones.
